title: Is the industry ripe for disruption?
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you decide whether an idea is a good one?

Here he is trying to think what to start next, Jose said. Is the idea a good idea or a bad idea? How do we develop a criteria? This is a great lesson, because it shows how his brain develops an idea from scratch.

A student said: first principles, then see if there is demand. Another said: scalability. Jose said all good criteria, and the more advanced we are in developing criteria the better. As a venture investor he sees twenty or thirty deals a day and reads five lines, not the plan.
He gave the clue: one word the person uses in the chapter. A student said it: the industry was ripe for disruption.

groups.heading: An industry is a table with four legs

lines.text: I always describe it in a simple way, Jose said: imagine an industry is a table with four legs. Everybody says: it's just a table. Then somebody says: this table is missing a leg. If I push on the corner that doesn't have a leg, the whole industry falls on the ground.

He gave an example from his own work in the nineties. On the old telecom networks, one lane carried voice, another data, another video. On converged networks they all went together, more efficiently. A call from one country to another cost a dollar sixty-five, he said, but the real cost was less than a cent.
I realized this was going to change how countries manage telecom, he said. The artificial long-distance rates were going to come way down, because the cost was less than a cent. That is disruption.

The same with banking, he said, in the person's thinking. Instead of many separate channels and trips to the ATM, converge everything on one platform. The money stays in the system, and think of the cash flow for whoever runs the system.

Students gave examples: a lodging platform, a ride app, an online store. Jose pushed: what industry is it displacing? That is the source of the opportunity. Hotels with a high cost structure, taxis, bookshops and retail.

We have to develop a fluency as entrepreneurs, he said, to look at something and say: this is an opportunity. I want you to see these opportunities all around us, because entrepreneurship is seeing what nobody else has seen.
What industry around you is missing a leg?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write an industry you know well.
Write the missing leg: the cost, delay or inefficiency everyone accepts.
Write what you would converge into one system.
Write who would lose money if you fixed it.
Write one product you use daily that disrupted another and what it displaced.

check.q: What word did the class give for what the person saw in the industry?
What image did Jose use for an industry?
What did Jose say is the source of the opportunity?

recap: Look for the industry's missing leg. See what it displaces.
